name: Work the VF-2's controls: find X and Y with an edge finder and set Z by handwheel, close both doors, Cycle Start and Feed Hold

working.role: the pendant: keys, the jog handle and Feed Hold; closes the right door

steadying.role: slides the paper under the tool while the working hand jogs Z; closes the left door; presses Cycle Start while the working hand covers Feed Hold; otherwise rests at the side

phases.what: Doors open, edge finder in the spindle. In MDI type S1200 M03 and press Cycle Start to spin it; then HANDLE JOG, the .01 increment and X [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the edge finder spinning; handle jog on X at .01

phases.what: The working hand from the keys to the jog handle
At .01 (each click 0.01 in), jog X, then Z (the Z key switches axis), to put the edge finder's tip beside the part's left edge, below its top and a little way off [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tip beside the edge, below the top, a few clicks off

phases.what: Switch to .001 and turn toward the edge slowly, a click at a time, eyes on the tip [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tip just trips off centre: the spindle centre is 0.100 in from the edge

phases.what: Z straight up until the finder clears the part, stopping with the handle's dial at zero [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the finder above the part, the dial at zero

phases.what: +X, exactly one full turn clockwise at .001: 100 clicks, 0.100 in [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the dial back at zero: the spindle centre over the edge

phases.what: OFFSET, page to the work offsets, cursor to G54 X, PART ZERO SET [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: G54 X holds the spindle's position

phases.what: Y the same way from the front edge: .01 to approach, .001 to the trip, Z up, one turn +Y, PART ZERO SET; then stop the spindle [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: G54 Y set and the spindle stopped

phases.what: With the tool in the spindle and X, Y over the part, jog Z down at .01 (or .1 where the shop allows it) to about 1 in above the top [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tool about 25 mm above the part

phases.what: The steadying hand lays a strip of paper on the part top under the tool, holding one end [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
Z down at .001, then .0001 near the paper, a click or a few at a time; between clicks the steadying hand slides the paper back and forth [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the paper drags under the tool but can still be moved

phases.what: The steadying hand's last slide of the paper, felt for drag [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: drag felt, the paper still moving

phases.what: OFFSET, page to the tool length offsets, cursor to the tool, TOOL OFFSET MEASURE; the steadying hand draws the paper out [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tool's length offset holds the machine Z

phases.what: Both hands out to the door handles, the doors standing open about 600 mm each, so the arms spread wide [proposed: duration_s]
Each hand closes on its door's handle [proposed: duration_s]
Pull both doors to the centre together, each sliding about 600 mm [proposed: force_n, travel_mm, duration_s, the 5 mm limit]
phases.ends_on: the doors meet, each within 5 mm of closed, which the interlock reads as shut

phases.what: Both hands let go and drop to the sides [proposed: duration_s]
The working hand's index to rest on Feed Hold; the steadying hand's index to Cycle Start
With the working hand resting on Feed Hold, the steadying hand presses Cycle Start [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
Watch the first approach, the finger still on Feed Hold; on a first run, stop when the tool is about 1 in above the part [proposed: duration_s]
phases.ends_on: the tool about 1 in above the part

phases.what: The working hand presses Feed Hold, then checks distance-to-go on the screen [proposed: force_n, duration_s]
phases.ends_on: all axis motion stops; the spindle keeps turning

phases.what: If distance-to-go agrees, the steadying hand presses Cycle Start again to resume [proposed: force_n, duration_s]

sources.ref: Haas Factory Outlet (Productivity Inc.), 'Haas Mill Operator' manual, rev. 8/2022, built from Haas's manuals with Haas's permission: general machine keys, setting tool length and work zero offsets, setup procedure, program proofing
sources.gives: Cycle Start starts a program; Feed Hold stops all axis motion while the spindle turns on; Cycle Start resumes, and only with the door closed; tool length offsets by handle jog at .1/.01/.001/.0001, touched off and loaded with TOOL OFFSET MEASURE; work offsets loaded with PART ZERO SET; on a first run, Feed Hold about 1 in in front of the part

sources.ref: Virasak and Kepka, Manufacturing Processes 4-5, Unit 6: Haas Control (Open Oregon Educational Resources, CC BY 4.0)
sources.gives: each click moves the selected increment; the edge finder at S1200: .01 to approach, .001 until it trips, Z up with the dial at zero, one full turn +X at .001 puts the spindle over the edge; the tool touched off on a sheet of paper that can still be moved; one hand on Feed Hold while Cycle Start is pressed

sources.ref: Kurt, 'Double Station Manual Vise Setup' (YouTube), measured locally with MediaPipe Hand Landmarker; borrowed, as no footage of this machine was tracked
sources.gives: reach durations: the right hand's interquartile range, 0.32-0.67 s

notes: One card for the VF-2 controls the G1 steps use, in the order the steps use them; the planner may want it split per control (jog and offsets, doors, cycle) once it sequences steps. Z is set here by handwheel touch-off on paper; the nist-ftc-10 plan names the Renishaw tool setter (tsetter) for Z, which needs its own card. Neither source corrects for the paper's thickness (the factory outlet's manual uses a feeler gauge). Cycle Start falls to the steadying hand because the textbook keeps one hand on Feed Hold while the other presses Cycle Start, and Feed Hold sits right of Cycle Start in the station. The station record has no jog handle or keypad yet: 'jog_handle' and 'keys' are names for the stations session to place. Proposed, with reasons (phase numbers count from 1): forces, since no source gives one: 3 N on the keys (#1, #7, #13), 1 N on the jog handle (#3 to #6, #8, #9, #11), 0.3 N laying and 0.5 N sliding the paper (#10, #12), 5 N on Cycle Start and Feed Hold (#19, #21, #22), as the station's proposed affordance force; the jog handle's grasp, fingertips round the rim, since no source shows how it is held; durations, since the sources give the order but no times: #1 6 s for about a dozen key presses, #3 and #4 3-8 s each, #5 2 s, #6 1.5 s for one turn, #7 and #13 3 s, #8 15-30 s for Y, #9 3-8 s, #10 1.5 s, #11 8-20 s, #12 1.0 s, #20 5-15 s, and 0.3 s a press for #19, #21 and #22; the door close, #14 to #17, which no source shows done two-handed: it is the brief's choice. Its reach (#14) takes 0.6-1.0 s because the arms spread about 1.2 m, wider than the footage's reaches; the grasp (#15) and release (#17) 0.3 s each; the pull (#16) 15 N per door over 600 mm in 1.0-1.5 s, ending within 5 mm of closed, which are the VF-2 station record's own proposed door friction, travel and door_closed_mm (moonshot/library/stations/vf2.json).
